evidence:
EditFaultPage.tsx renders three hardcoded English strings with NO i18n on a react-i18next multi-locale app: line 35 '← Back to Fault' (button), line 37

Edit Fault

, lines 38-40 'Update the fault details. Note: editing is only available before the fault is triaged.' The file contains ZERO useTranslation()/t() calls (grep count 0).

This is a MISSED page, not an accepted codebase pattern: every sibling in the same faults feature is localized — CreateFaultPage.tsx (6 t() calls), FaultDetailPage.tsx (79), FaultReportsPage.tsx (28), FaultsPage.tsx (3), and the shared child FaultForm.tsx (41). EditFaultPage was the only faults page overlooked during localization, so non-English (sk/cs/de) managers editing a fault see three English-only strings in an otherwise translated flow (Epic 4 / UC-03.1).

Impact: LOW (i18n gap on a user-facing manager page). Confidence MEDIUM: the hardcoded strings are directly in the unconditional render and the zero-t() count is confirmed statically; not runtime-reproduced and route-reachability from the fault-detail 'edit' action assumed but not traced. Fresh vs backlog: no prior faults-* finding exists in the ppt-web-ui corpus (faults feature was entirely unmined before this pass). Fix (cloud-landable, ppt-web frontend): wrap the three strings in t('...') with keys under the faults namespace, mirroring CreateFaultPage/FaultDetailPage.

RequestSignatureModal.tsx:214-221 — the e-sign request error alert renders the RAW error message for any Error instance: `{createRequest.error instanceof Error ? createRequest.error.message : t('common.unknownError', 'An error occurred. Please try again.')}`. Only the non-Error branch is localized; the common case (an ApiError from the createRequest mutation extends Error) shows its raw, untranslated .message (e.g. 'Request failed with status 400' / a server-supplied English string) directly to the user on a multi-locale (sk/cs/de/en) app.

The error IS surfaced (role='alert', styled), so this is not a silent-failure — it is a localization/UX gap: sk/cs/de users get an English/technical error string for a common failure (e.g. requesting a signature on an ineligible lease) instead of a translated message. This mirrors an established recurring class in the ppt-web-ui corpus (code-review-ppt-web-ui-emergency-dir-raw-err-message, code-review-ppt-web-ui-errorboundary-raw-message-prod) but is a distinct, previously-unmined instance in the leases feature (UC e-sign / lease signature flow).

Impact: LOW (untranslated/technical error text on a user-facing modal). Confidence MEDIUM: the raw-message branch is confirmed statically; the exact server message contents were not runtime-inspected. Fix (cloud-landable, ppt-web frontend): map known mutation error statuses to translated keys (t('leases.esign.errors.*')) and fall back to t('common.unknownError') rather than error.message, or run error.message through an i18n message-resolver.
